blueprint.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

item.vignette: A 3-year-old girl is evaluated for developmental regression. She developed normally during the first year of life but then lost purposeful hand use and spoken words. She now has repetitive hand-wringing movements, impaired gait, and deceleration of head growth. Genetic testing identifies a de novo pathogenic variant in MECP2.
item.lead_in: Loss of which normal molecular function most directly contributes to this patient's disorder?

options.A: Peroxisomal import of very-long-chain fatty acids
options.B: Production of survival motor neuron protein from SMN1
options.C: Expression of the active maternal UBE3A allele in neurons
options.D: Production of frataxin from the FXN gene
options.E: Regulation of neuronal gene expression by methyl-CpG-binding protein 2

item.tested_construct: Molecular function disrupted in Rett syndrome

explanation.key_explanation: Classic Rett syndrome is usually caused by loss-of-function MECP2 variants. MeCP2 is a methyl-CpG-binding protein involved in regulating gene activity in the brain and maintaining normal neuronal function and synaptic connectivity.

distractor_explanations.A: ABCD1-dependent peroxisomal VLCFA transport is disrupted in X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy.
distractor_explanations.B: SMN1 deficiency causes spinal muscular atrophy.
distractor_explanations.C: Loss of maternal UBE3A expression causes Angelman syndrome and is an imprinting disorder distinct from Rett syndrome.
distractor_explanations.D: Reduced frataxin production causes Friedreich ataxia.
distractor_explanations.E: Correct. MECP2 encodes a methyl-CpG-binding protein involved in regulation of neuronal gene expression.

explanation.educational_objective: Recognize Rett syndrome as an MECP2-related neurodevelopmental disorder caused by impaired methyl-CpG-dependent regulation of neuronal gene expression.

evidence_map.claim: ABCD1 mediates peroxisomal VLCFA transport and is defective in X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy.
SMN1 produces SMN protein and loss causes spinal muscular atrophy.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not explain developmental regression with MECP2 mutation.

evidence_map.claim: In CNS neurons the maternal UBE3A allele is active, and loss causes Angelman syndrome.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Distinct imprinting disorder from Rett syndrome.

evidence_map.claim: FXN GAA expansion reduces frataxin production and causes Friedreich ataxia.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not fit the developmental-regression phenotype or MECP2 genotype.

evidence_map.claim: MECP2 encodes MeCP2, which participates in regulation of gene activity and normal neuronal function; pathogenic variants cause Rett syndrome.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Directly explains the patient's regression and stereotypic hand movements.

sources.title: Rett syndrome: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: Classic Rett syndrome is usually caused by MECP2 variants; MeCP2 participates in regulation of gene activity and normal neuronal function.

sources.title: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: ABCD1 encodes ALDP, which transports very-long-chain fatty acids into peroxisomes; deficiency disrupts VLCFA breakdown and causes accumulation toxic to myelin and adrenal cortex.

sources.title: Spinal muscular atrophy: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: SMN1 mutations cause SMA; SMN2 copy number modifies severity because additional SMN2 copies produce more functional SMN protein.

sources.title: Angelman syndrome: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: In CNS neurons, the maternal UBE3A copy is active; loss of maternal UBE3A function causes Angelman syndrome.

sources.title: Friedreich ataxia: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: FXN GAA repeat expansion reduces frataxin production; frataxin is important for normal mitochondrial function.
